name: Measure-theoretic density of the set A in the complement
notes:
Auto-designed from: Design an Ob3ect for:

Measure-theoretic density of the set A in the complement of a maximal sum-free set S

phase_0.boundary_condition: The ambient measurable space containing the set A and the maximal sum-free set S
phase_0.domain_name: Measure-theoretic density of the set A in the complement
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.justification: The forward transformation of a set into its numerical measure

AREV.justification: The mapping from a measure value back to a candidate set of points

CLINK.justification: The sequential composition of the set A with the complement of S

ENGAGR.justification: A point where every neighborhood contains both A and its complement in equal measure-theoretic weight

EVALF.justification: The condition where the local measure ratio approaches zero

EVALT.justification: The condition where the local measure ratio approaches unity

FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of the original measurable space from S and its complement

FSPLIT.justification: The division of the space into the sum-free set S and its complement S-prime

IFIX.justification: The final scalar result appended to the mathematical record

IMSCRIB.justification: The identity mapping that identifies points as belonging to the set without transformation

TANCH.justification: The final value representing the density of A in the complement of S

VINIT.justification: The initial state before the definition of any sets or measure assignments

phase_3.both_description: The point is a Lebesgue point for both A and its complement
phase_3.false_description: The set A is locally sparse within the complement of S
phase_3.true_description: The set A is locally dense within the complement of S
phase_3.void_description: The null set with measure zero

steps.domain_action: identify the set A within X
partition X into S and S-prime
apply the Lebesgue measure to the intersection
branch on the limit of the measure ratio at point x
point x is a density point of A in S-prime
point x is not a density point
discard the point from the density calculation
point x lies on the measure-theoretic boundary
rejoin S and S-prime to verify the total measure

phase_5.alfs_store: The axioms of Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory with Choice
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The limit process as the neighborhood radius approaches zero

phase_6.cycle_cost: The computational complexity of the limit operation
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The information content of the set is preserved through the measure-theoretic mapping
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A fixed scalar value in the interval [0, 1]
